parameters.content:
## Monitor hotel reviews on Tripadvisor and route the bad ones

No reputation management subscription and no review platform API key. Every week this pulls the latest reviews for each hotel you list, then **splits them down two paths**: every review lands in a running history tab, and anything at or below your rating threshold is also queued on a separate tab so nobody has to scan the sheet to find the complaints.

Because each run appends a dated snapshot keyed by review ID, a review ID in this week's rows that is missing from last week's is a new review, and the running review total on every row shows the pace at which they arrive.

**Who's it for**
Hotel managers who want to see a bad review before the front desk hears about it, agencies reporting on guest feedback for client properties, and teams watching a competitor's reviews next to their own.

**How it works**
1. A schedule trigger fires once a week
2. One Set node holds the hotels you watch and your alert threshold
3. The Apify node fetches the latest reviews for each hotel
4. A Code node keys each row by review ID and marks the ones needing a reply
5. An IF node routes those to their own tab, while the history tab gets everything

**Setup**
1. Create a free Apify account and add your API token to the Apify credential
2. Connect your Google account in both Sheets nodes and pick a spreadsheet
3. Replace the example place ID with your own hotels. The place ID is the number after d in the hotel page URL

**Make it yours**
Three optional nodes sit unconnected at the bottom of the canvas. Drag a connection from the true branch of **Is this a bad review?** into any of them to add Slack, email, or once-only alerting. Nothing else has to change.

**Good to know**
A review costs about a fifth of a cent, so checking the latest ten reviews on one hotel weekly is just under 2 cents a week.
Actor: https://apify.com/johnvc/tripadvisor-api?fpr=9n7kx3&fp_sid=n8n

### 1. Schedule
Runs every Monday morning. Change the cadence, or swap in a manual trigger while you test.

### 2. Your input
The hotels to watch as place IDs, how many of the latest reviews to pull, and the rating that counts as bad. This is the only node you edit.

### 3. Fan out
Turns your hotel list into one review lookup each.

### 4. Fetch
Runs the Tripadvisor API actor in reviews mode for one hotel. Add your Apify credential here.

### 5. Clean
Keeps only real review rows, so an upstream error never reaches the sheet.

### 6. Shape
One row per review, keyed by review ID and stamped with the run date, marking anything at or below your threshold.

### 7. Route
Bad reviews take the true branch and also carry on to the history, so nothing is lost. This is the branch to hang an alert off.

### 8. Deliver
Two tabs in one spreadsheet: a reply queue holding only the bad reviews, and a history holding every review. Columns map automatically.

### New reviews are a sheet diff
Every run appends a dated snapshot keyed by review ID. An ID that appears this week and was not there last week is a new review, and the Total reviews column rising tells you the pace.

### Finding a place ID
Open the hotel's Tripadvisor page and read the number after d in the URL: a URL containing d143336 means place ID 143336. The actor's search mode returns the same placeId for every hotel it finds, so you can look properties up by name once and paste the IDs here.

### Why two tabs
A single appended log buries the complaints among the five star reviews. Splitting at the IF gives the front desk a short reply queue while the history tab still holds everything for reporting. Change the threshold in the input node to make the queue stricter or wider.

### Prefer a dedicated node?
There is a community node for this actor: `n8n-nodes-tripadvisor-api`. Install it from Settings then Community nodes if you would rather configure Tripadvisor with typed fields than a JSON body. This template uses the official verified Apify node so it runs on n8n Cloud with nothing to install.

## Optional add-ons, not wired up

These three are deliberately left unconnected. Pick the ones that match how your team wants to hear about a bad review, drag a connection into them from the **true** output of **Is this a bad review?**, and delete the rest.

**Only the first time you see it** stops the same review alerting every week, because the run re-reads the latest reviews each time. **Slack** posts into a channel. **Gmail** emails whoever is on duty. Each needs its own credential before it will run.
